title: Catalyst query compilation in Fabric Spark
purpose: Catalyst query compilation. Parsed logical plan; Analyzed logical plan; Optimized logical plan; Physical plan; Whole-stage code generation.
accessibleSummary: Catalyst query compilation. Parsed logical plan; Analyzed logical plan; Optimized logical plan; Physical plan; Whole-stage code generation.
longDescription: Catalyst query compilation. Parsed logical plan; Analyzed logical plan; Optimized logical plan; Physical plan; Whole-stage code generation.

nodes.label: 1. Parsed logical plan
nodes.summary: The query becomes an unresolved operator tree; names are not yet checked.
nodes.detail: The query becomes an unresolved operator tree; names are not yet checked.
nodes.whyItMatters: The query becomes an unresolved operator tree; names are not yet checked.

evidence.note: EXPLAIN EXTENDED prints the parsed logical plan with names still unresolved.

inputs: DataFrame API calls or SQL text
drill.example: orders.filter(amount > 100).join(customers, "cust_id") parses to a tree whose relations are still the strings 'orders' and 'customers'.
failureModes: A syntax error stops the query here, before any catalog lookup.

nodes.label: 2. Analyzed logical plan
nodes.summary: Catalog resolution binds relations and columns to real schemas and types.
nodes.detail: Catalog resolution binds relations and columns to real schemas and types.
nodes.whyItMatters: Catalog resolution binds relations and columns to real schemas and types.

evidence.note: The analyzed plan binds relations and attributes to real typed objects.

drill.example: 'orders' resolves to a Delta relation with typed columns order_id, cust_id and amount.
failureModes: A misspelled column raises AnalysisException before optimization runs.

nodes.label: 3. Optimized logical plan
nodes.summary: Rule-based rewrites including predicate pushdown and column pruning.
nodes.detail: Rule-based rewrites including predicate pushdown and column pruning.
nodes.whyItMatters: Rule-based rewrites including predicate pushdown and column pruning.

evidence.note: The optimized logical plan is produced by rule-based rewrites after analysis.
Predicate pushdown and column pruning reduce what the scan reads.

drill.example: A filter on amount is pushed into the Parquet reader and unused columns never leave storage — visible as PushedFilters and a narrowed ReadSchema.
controls: Predicate must not wrap the column in a cast or UDF
failureModes: PushedFilters:[] means pushdown failed and the scan reads everything.

nodes.label: 4. Physical plan
nodes.summary: Candidate physical plans are costed and one algorithm is chosen.
nodes.detail: Candidate physical plans are costed and one algorithm is chosen.
nodes.whyItMatters: Candidate physical plans are costed and one algorithm is chosen.

evidence.note: COST mode prints the statistics that explain why the optimizer chose a join strategy.
autoBroadcastJoinThreshold defaults to 10 MB and governs the broadcast decision.

drill.example: A join whose smaller side is estimated under 10 MB is planned as BroadcastHashJoin rather than SortMergeJoin.
failureModes: A stale or absent statistic produces a sort-merge join where a broadcast would have been far cheaper.

nodes.label: 5. Whole-stage code generation
nodes.summary: Operators are fused into one generated Java function per stage.
nodes.detail: Operators are fused into one generated Java function per stage.
nodes.whyItMatters: Operators are fused into one generated Java function per stage.

evidence.note: CODEGEN mode prints the generated code alongside the physical plan.

processing: Emit and compile Java per stage
drill.example: A filter and a projection compile into one loop with no virtual call between them, shown as a *(1) prefix in the plan.
failureModes: A Python UDF in the middle of a stage breaks fusion and the *(n) prefixes disappear.

nodes.label: Native path branches after this
nodes.summary: Native execution engages after planning and preserves optimizer behaviour.
nodes.detail: Native execution engages after planning and preserves optimizer behaviour.
nodes.whyItMatters: Native execution engages after planning and preserves optimizer behaviour.

evidence.note: NEE preserves adaptive query execution, cost-based rewrites, column pruning and predicate pushdown.
Native execution is toggled per application with spark.native.enabled.

outputs: Native or JVM execution per operator
drill.example: A scan and aggregation offload to Velox while an unsupported window function stays on the JVM.
failureModes: An unsupported expression drops the whole enclosing operator back to the JVM.

edges.label: Catalog resolution binds names to schemas
Rule-based rewrites run on the resolved tree
Stage operators fuse into generated Java
Supported operators route to the native path
